questions.stem: Regarding failover group membership, which statement is correct?

options.text: An object can belong to multiple failover groups simultaneously
An object can only be in one failover group
An object must be in at least two failover groups for redundancy
Failover groups cannot contain database objects

explanation.correct: An object can only be in one failover group.

distractors.A: An object cannot belong to multiple failover groups; it is limited to one.
distractors.C: There is no requirement to place an object in two failover groups.
distractors.D: Failover groups can contain database objects among others.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about object membership in replication and failover groups are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: An object can be in both a failover group and a replication group at the same time
An object can be in multiple replication groups all targeting the same account
An object can be in multiple replication groups if each group replicates to a different target account
An object cannot be in both a failover group and a replication group
Replication groups cannot target more than one account in total

explanation.correct: An object can be in multiple replication groups as long as each group replicates to a different target account, and an object cannot be in both a failover group and a replication group.

distractors.A: An object cannot be in both a failover group and a replication group.
distractors.B: Multiple replication groups for the same object must each target a different account, not the same one.
distractors.E: Replication groups can replicate to one or more target accounts; this statement is incorrect.

questions.scenario: A provider account has an inbound share (from another provider) and an outbound share it created. The team wants to replicate shares.

options.text: Only outbound shares; inbound shares (from providers) cannot be replicated
Only inbound shares
Both inbound and outbound shares equally
Neither; shares are never replicable

explanation.correct: You can only replicate outbound shares. Replication of inbound shares (shares from providers) is not supported.

distractors.C: Only outbound shares replicate, not both.
distractors.D: Outbound shares are replicable; share replication is available on all editions.

questions.scenario: An administrator is planning how many replication or failover groups can contain account objects other than databases and shares.
questions.stem: Which TWO statements are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: An account can have unlimited groups containing account-level objects
Account object replication is available on Standard Edition
An account can have only one replication or failover group that contains objects other than databases or shares
Account objects cannot be replicated at all
Account object (other than database and share) replication requires Business Critical Edition or higher

explanation.correct: An account can have only one replication/failover group containing non-database/share objects, and replicating such account objects requires Business Critical Edition or higher.

distractors.A: Only one such group is allowed per account, not unlimited.
distractors.B: Account object replication is not available on Standard Edition.
distractors.D: Account objects can be replicated (with Business Critical Edition or higher).

questions.scenario: A security admin is granting replication-related privileges to roles.
questions.stem: Which THREE are valid replication privileges/grants in Snowflake? (Select THREE)

options.text: REPLICATE ACROSS REGIONS
CREATE REPLICATION GROUP (on the account)
PROMOTE PRIMARY
CREATE FAILOVER GROUP (on the account)
ENABLE DISASTER RECOVERY
FAILOVER (on a failover group)

explanation.correct: Valid replication privileges include CREATE REPLICATION GROUP and CREATE FAILOVER GROUP (on the account, granted by ACCOUNTADMIN) and FAILOVER (on a failover group, to promote a secondary to primary).

distractors.A: REPLICATE ACROSS REGIONS is not a defined Snowflake privilege.
distractors.C: PROMOTE PRIMARY is not a privilege name; promotion uses the FAILOVER privilege.
distractors.E: ENABLE DISASTER RECOVERY is not a Snowflake privilege.

questions.scenario: A team uses the legacy ALTER DATABASE ... ENABLE REPLICATION TO ACCOUNTS method to manage database replication and failover.
questions.stem: Which role is required to enable and manage this database replication?

options.text: SYSADMIN
SECURITYADMIN
ACCOUNTADMIN
USERADMIN

explanation.correct: For database replication, only a user with the ACCOUNTADMIN role can enable and manage database replication and failover.

distractors.A: SYSADMIN manages warehouses and objects but is not required for database replication management.
distractors.B: SECURITYADMIN manages grants and security, not database replication enablement.
distractors.D: USERADMIN manages users and roles, not database replication.

questions.scenario: An administrator holds the OWNERSHIP privilege on a failover group and needs to allow another role to promote a secondary to primary.

options.text: Grant or revoke the FAILOVER privilege on the group to that role
Only ACCOUNTADMIN can ever grant FAILOVER, regardless of ownership
Transfer the primary role automatically without any grant
Nothing; FAILOVER cannot be delegated

explanation.correct: The FAILOVER privilege can be granted or revoked by a role with the OWNERSHIP privilege on the group, allowing delegation of the promote-to-primary capability.

distractors.B: A role with OWNERSHIP on the group (not only ACCOUNTADMIN) can grant FAILOVER.
distractors.C: Promotion requires the FAILOVER privilege and an explicit ALTER command, not automatic transfer.
distractors.D: FAILOVER can be delegated by the group owner.

questions.scenario: A platform engineer lists the high-level workflow steps to configure account replication and failover for disaster recovery.
questions.stem: Which THREE steps are part of the replication configuration workflow? (Select THREE)

options.text: Convert the source account to Standard Edition
Disable Time Travel across all accounts
Enable replication across a set of accounts in the same organization
Create a primary failover group specifying objects and target accounts
Create at least one secondary failover group and refresh it
Delete the primary account after the first refresh

explanation.correct: The workflow enables replication across accounts in the organization, creates a primary failover group (defining objects and target accounts), and creates at least one secondary failover group that is then refreshed on a schedule.

distractors.A: Converting to Standard Edition would remove failover capabilities (which need Business Critical).
distractors.B: Disabling Time Travel is not part of the replication workflow.
distractors.F: The primary account is not deleted; it remains as the source.

questions.scenario: After creating a secondary failover group, an administrator wants to keep it current with the latest changes from the primary.

options.text: A one-time manual failover
An initial refresh plus a regular refresh schedule
A permanent read-write lock on the secondary
Automatic promotion of the secondary each day

explanation.correct: You perform an initial refresh and set up a schedule to regularly bring the latest changes to each secondary account, keeping replicas synchronized.

distractors.A: Failover promotes a secondary to primary; it is not how you keep a replica current.
distractors.C: Secondaries are read-only replicas; a read-write lock is not the sync mechanism.
distractors.D: Daily automatic promotion would repeatedly fail over, which is not the goal of keeping a replica current.

questions.scenario: A DBA clones a database that contains a database role, then tries to clone the same database role again into the target database.
questions.stem: What happens on the second clone attempt?

options.text: It succeeds and overwrites the existing role
The command fails because the database role is already cloned in the target
It creates a duplicate role with a suffix
It silently skips the role

explanation.correct: If the database role is already cloned to the target database, the command fails; you must drop the database role from the target and retry the CLONE command.

distractors.A: It does not overwrite; the command fails.
distractors.D: It does not silently skip; it returns a failure.

questions.scenario: A developer clones a database and inspects whether object parameters explicitly set on the source were retained.
questions.stem: What is true about parameter inheritance in the clone?

options.text: All parameters reset to account defaults in the clone
Parameters are never carried to clones
Only security parameters are retained
Parameters explicitly set on the source are retained in the clones

explanation.correct: Parameters that are explicitly set on a source database, schema, or table are retained in any clones created from the source container or its child objects.

distractors.A: Explicitly set source parameters are retained, not reset to account defaults.
distractors.B: Parameters are carried to clones when explicitly set on the source.
distractors.C: The behavior applies to object parameters generally, not only security parameters.

questions.scenario: A team clones a database that contains hybrid tables and wants the clone to include everything except hybrid tables.

options.text: IGNORE TABLES WITH INSUFFICIENT DATA RETENTION
IGNORE HYBRID TABLES
INCLUDE INTERNAL STAGES
COPY GRANTS

explanation.correct: IGNORE HYBRID TABLES skips hybrid tables when cloning a database or schema; the cloned object includes other objects but omits hybrid tables.

distractors.A: IGNORE TABLES WITH INSUFFICIENT DATA RETENTION skips tables purged from Time Travel, not hybrid tables.
distractors.C: INCLUDE INTERNAL STAGES adds internal stages; it does not skip hybrid tables.
distractors.D: COPY GRANTS copies privileges, unrelated to hybrid tables.

questions.scenario: A developer clones a schema (not the whole database) that contains a table which references a sequence located in a DIFFERENT schema.
questions.stem: Which sequence does the cloned table reference?

options.text: A cloned copy of the sequence in the new schema
The source sequence in the other schema
No sequence; the default is removed
A newly generated sequence with a random name

explanation.correct: Because the sequence is defined in a different schema that is not cloned together with the table, the cloned table references the source sequence.

distractors.A: A cloned sequence is referenced only when the container holding both is cloned together.
distractors.C: The default is retained, referencing the source sequence.

questions.scenario: A compliance team reviews which advanced replication features their Business Critical account can use that Enterprise cannot.
questions.stem: Which THREE replication-related features require Business Critical Edition (or higher)? (Select THREE)

options.text: Share replication
Dataset replication
Database replication
Cortex Search Service replication
Replication Group
Data protected with Tri-Secret Secure

explanation.correct: Dataset replication, Cortex Search Service replication, and Tri-Secret Secure data protection all require Business Critical Edition or higher.

distractors.A: Share replication is available on all editions including Standard.
distractors.C: Database replication is available on all editions including Standard.
distractors.E: Replication Group is available on all editions including Standard.

questions.scenario: An architect combines Client Redirect with account replication for disaster recovery and reviews the constraints.
questions.stem: Which TWO constraints apply to Client Redirect connections? (Select TWO)

options.text: The primary and secondary connections may share the same region
The connection URL must be changed by clients during failover
The accounts storing the primary and secondary connections must be in different regions
The secondary connection is created as a replica of the primary
Client Redirect works only within a single account

explanation.correct: The accounts storing primary and secondary connections must be in different regions, and the secondary connection is created as a replica of the primary (CREATE CONNECTION ... AS REPLICA OF ...).

distractors.A: Primary and secondary connection accounts must be in different regions.
distractors.B: Clients keep using the same connection URL during failover; they do not change it.
distractors.E: Client Redirect spans multiple accounts across regions, not a single account.

questions.scenario: A FinOps analyst maps out which cross-region/cross-cloud operations incur Snowflake data transfer charges.
questions.stem: Which THREE operations can incur data transfer (egress) costs when they cross a region or cloud boundary? (Select THREE)

options.text: Using external functions to transfer data to AWS/Azure/Google
External network access from UDF/procedure handler code
Querying data entirely within the same region
PUT calls (FileOperation.put) to external stages from stored procedures
Retrieving query results across regions via a client driver
Loading data into Snowflake (ingress)

explanation.correct: External functions, external network access from handler code, and PUT calls (FileOperation.put) to external stages can incur data transfer costs when crossing region/cloud boundaries.

distractors.C: Data transfers within the same region are free.
distractors.E: Snowflake does not charge egress when a client/driver retrieves query results across regions or clouds.
distractors.F: Snowflake does not charge data ingress fees for loading data.

questions.scenario: A database and share replication setup must span from a Snowflake commercial region to a Virtual Private Snowflake (VPS) region, which are in different region groups.
questions.stem: What is required to enable this?

options.text: Nothing; all region groups replicate freely
Downgrade both accounts to Standard Edition
Contact Snowflake Support to enable cross-region-group replication
Use Client Redirect instead of replication

explanation.correct: To replicate between regions in different region groups (e.g., commercial to government or VPS), you must contact Snowflake Support; replication within a region group works by default.

distractors.A: Cross-region-group replication is not automatic; it requires contacting Snowflake Support.
distractors.B: Edition downgrade does not enable cross-region-group replication and removes features.
distractors.D: Client Redirect handles client connections, not object replication across region groups.
